items.label: Eikon Therapeutics Cantor conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CEO Roger Perlmutter on the super-resolution microscopy platform

set.signal: CEO Roger Perlmutter on the super-resolution microscopy platform, which he calls over the long term the most important source of value for the company (though a minority of expense, since clinical trial expenses are significant for a late-stage company): Eikon's entirely proprietary instruments evaluate millions of cells per day and typically 10 to 100,000 proteins per cell, imaging usually at about 100 frames per second (frame rates higher than 1,000 frames per second are possible) with roughly 10-millisecond time resolution and roughly 10 to 30 nanometer spatial resolution. When the instruments are all running full tilt, which they often are, Eikon produces on the order of a petabyte of data a day; he calls it one of the largest data producers in the world. Screening assays can screen 1 million compounds or so in roughly 6 weeks, and the Werner helicase inhibitor went from the initial lead to a development candidate in about 16 months. The novel androgen receptor antagonist, originally planned for an IND filing in 2027, will now have its IND filed before the end of this year because the analysis was done so fast. CEO: the tools will let Eikon bring forward important new molecules much more rapidly.

items.reason: The Investing.com transcript's 'Milpitas' conflicts with the company's own filing (headquarters in Millbrae, California, already on the node) and is most likely a transcription error; the location is not a captured fact, so it is dropped rather than recorded as a second, conflicting site.
items.evidence: little Eikon in Milpitas, California, is one of the largest data producers in the world (8-K 08-13-2026: 'its current corporate headquarters in Millbrae, California')

items.label: Eikon Therapeutics Cantor conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CEO on the selective PARP1 inhibitors: Eikon searched

set.signal: CEO on the selective PARP1 inhibitors: Eikon searched for the most selective PARP1 inhibitors and found a set of molecules at a small company called IMPACT in China; it filed the INDs and advanced two of them. The non-brain-penetrant EIK-1003, the most advanced, is about 650-fold selective for PARP1 over PARP2 and has been used to treat more than 250 patients, showing less myelosuppression than dual PARP1/PARP2 inhibitors; the brain-penetrant EIK-1004 is about 800-fold selective at the enzymatic level, has been studied in around 75 patients and has completed multiple ascending dose studies, which he says support the hypothesis that selective PARP1 inhibition spares the hematopoietic system. CEO: to his knowledge combining a PARP inhibitor with full-dose paclitaxel had never been possible before (he says they tried very hard with LYNPARZA and could not); this could take PARP inhibitors beyond maintenance into second-line and possibly first-line treatment (for first-line with platinum 'We have no data there'); he calls Eikon's PARP inhibitors 'certainly the most advanced, highly selective PARP1 inhibitors right now in clinical development'.

items.reason: The individual's name is a personnel detail with no bearing on the fact and its machine-transcribed spelling is unverifiable; the licensor stays as the CEO named it ('a small company called IMPACT in China').
items.evidence: we found a set of molecules at a small company called IMPACT in China, run by Dr. Tsai, whom I'd known in a previous life, a medicinal chemist.
